# Point-in-time analysis: 2025 and 2026 Weeks 1–9, and the Week 10 forecast

*Generated by `research/season_analysis.py` on Nov 14, 2026. Every game and every player is evaluated as if its week hadn't been played: features use only the closing line, the schedule, results and play-by-play from **earlier weeks** (plus the previous season at quarter weight), and that week's pre-game injury report and roster. Outcomes are used only to grade.*

**Samples.** 2026 Weeks 1–9: 136 games. 2025 Weeks 1–9: 135 games (a second, independent sample used to check whether a 2026 finding repeats). Player-level picks: 2026 only (see §4).

**Reading the numbers.** Every rate shows its count. ⚠ marks a rate resting on fewer than 15 observations: treat it as preliminary. Against the spread or a total, 50% is a coin flip and **52.4%** is the break-even rate at standard −110 prices. The 90% interval (Wilson) and the two-sided p-value test against 50%. About 20 signal/slot combinations are tested here, so one or two will look 'significant' at p < 0.10 by chance alone.

## 1. Which data signals would have improved picks

Each signal takes a side only when it has a real opinion (threshold in the table); otherwise it passes. *r* is the correlation between the signal's raw value and the result against the line across every game it covers (a scale-free check that doesn't depend on the threshold).

### Rest, in more detail

Rest was the only game-level signal whose correlation with covering pointed the same way in both seasons (2026 r = +0.33, n = 136, p = 0.000; 2025 r = +0.17, n = 135, p = 0.04). But the simple '3+ days' rule went 21-9 in 2026 and only 12-13 in 2025, and the effect is concentrated in a few bye-week games, so it is **promising but preliminary**, not a proven edge.

| Home team's rest vs opponent | Games | Home covered | Avg home result vs line |
|---|---|---|---|
| Home team 7+ fewer days (opponent off a bye) | 10 | 20.0% (2/10) ⚠ | -8.3 |
| Home team 1–6 fewer days | 38 | 40.5% (15/37) | -3.7 |
| Same rest | 179 | 46.3% (81/175) | -0.2 |
| Home team 1–6 more days | 31 | 60.0% (18/30) | +3.5 |
| Home team 7+ more days (off a bye) | 13 | 69.2% (9/13) ⚠ | +8.8 |

### Player-level signals (anytime TD)

These were ranked earlier with the same point-in-time method on every 2026 Week 1–9 player-game (n = 3,261) and re-checked on 2025 Weeks 10–18; the full table is in `docs/BACKTEST_W1_9.md` §3. Gain = how much the input improved the model's log loss (×10⁻³ per player-game, 90% interval). Higher is better; an interval that crosses 0 is not established.

| Rank | Input | 2026 W1–9 gain | 2025 W10–18 repeat | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Team expected TDs (from spread + total) × player's carry/target share | +46.0 [28.0, 64.7] vs TD history alone | core | **Strong, replicated** |
| 2 | Pre-game depth-chart rank | +2.8 [0.3, 5.4] | +3.1 [0.9, 5.4] | **Real, small** (mostly RBs) |
| 3 | Goal-line rushing role (inside-5 and goal-to-go share, QB runs) | +2.3 [0.4, 4.2] | +2.4 [0.8, 3.9] | **Real, small** (RBs, QBs) |
| 4 | Player's own TD rate | +1.6 [−0.2, 3.4] | +1.8 [0.5, 3.1] | Probably real, small |
| 5 | Snap share and estimated routes | +1.2 [−0.2, 2.7] | +1.0 [−0.6, 2.5] | Not established |
| 6 | End-zone / red-zone targets, long-TD history | +0.3 to +0.4 | ≈ 0 | Noise |
| 7 | Opponent matchup (TDs allowed by position) | −0.3 | −1.2 [−2.1, −0.4] | **Hurt** in both seasons |
| 8 | Injuries beyond removing Out players; recent role change; efficiency | −0.3 to −1.0 | ≈ 0 | No help for the chance (still needed to remove Out players) |

- Implied team points vs actual: correlation **0.40** (n = 542 team-games). A team's score landed within 3 points of its implied total 24.5% (133/542) of the time and within 7 points 58.3% (316/542). The average miss of 7.3 points per team is about one and a half touchdowns: the line gets the *order* of teams right far more reliably than the exact score.
- Final margins of exactly 3: 14.4% (39/271); exactly 7: 8.9% (24/271); 3 or fewer: 24.0% (65/271).

### Did the gap between implied and actual scores predict anything?

- **Point-in-time test.** A team's average gap over its previous 3 games (scored minus implied) vs its next game: correlation with the next gap **-0.09** (n = 478, p = 0.04); with next week's cover margin **-0.07** (n = 478, p = 0.15). Teams that had been beating their implied totals did not keep doing it at a rate the market missed.
- **Same-game (descriptive only, not a pick).** Teams that beat their implied points covered 73.0% (200/274). This is close to automatic (scoring more than expected usually means covering) and can't be known before kickoff.

## 4. Player-level hit rates: each team's highest-chance anytime-TD pick

**Prop lines.** Historical player prop lines (yards, receptions, anytime-TD prices) are **not** in the data, apart from the family's own anytime-TD prices for Weeks 2–4, so 'players most likely to exceed a prop line' can't be graded. This section uses the app's market, anytime TD: for each team and week, the player with the highest pre-game chance from model usage-v0.3c refit on earlier weeks only, skipping players listed Out or Doubtful. A pick whose player didn't take a snap is **void** (as a sportsbook would treat it) and left out of the hit rate.

### By week (2026)

| 2 | 32 | 1 | 31 | 12 | 38.7% (12/31) | 48.1% | 14.9 |
| 3 | 32 | 0 | 32 | 11 | 34.4% (11/32) | 46.0% | 14.7 |

| 8 | 28 | 1 | 27 | 14 | 51.9% (14/27) | 46.8% | 12.6 |
| 9 | 30 | 0 | 30 | 11 | 36.7% (11/30) | 47.1% | 14.1 |
| **All** | 272 | 5 | 267 | 125 | **46.8% (125/267, 90% CI 42%–52%)** | 45.9% | 122.6 |

**Aggregate:** the top pick per team scored 46.8% (125/267, 90% CI 42%–52%); the model expected 45.9% (122.6 hits vs 125 actual), so its chances were about right (within ±2 standard deviations = ±15.9 hits). A typical anytime-TD price on these players would need to be about +114 or longer to break even at this hit rate (≈ the American odds equal to the hit rate).

**Prime-time check.** In 2026 the top pick scored far more often in prime time (68.5% (37/54)) than the model expected. To see whether that repeats, the same comparison was run on 2025 with a rule that needs no model: each team's lead back (most carries in earlier weeks of the season; void if he didn't play).

| Season | Prime time (TNF/SNF/MNF) | All other games |
|---|---|---|
| 2026 | 63.6% (28/44, 90% CI 51%–74%) | 37.8% (65/172, 90% CI 32%–44%) |
| 2025 | 39.0% (41/105, 90% CI 32%–47%) | 42.0% (148/352, 90% CI 38%–46%) |
| 2025, Weeks 2–9 only | 36.5% (19/52, 90% CI 26%–48%) | 45.7% (75/164, 90% CI 39%–52%) |

It **did not repeat** in 2025 (lead backs scored slightly *less* in prime time), so the 2026 prime-time jump is most likely a small-sample streak, not something to build picks on.

**Top 10 chances league-wide each week:** scored 62.2% (56/90, 90% CI 54%–70%); model expected 57.3%.

## Summary: the strongest signals and how much to trust them

| Signal | What the evidence shows | Confidence |
|---|---|---|
| **Team implied points (from spread + total)** | Best single predictor of who scores: team TDs rise steadily with implied points (§3), and team expectation × player share is the core of the TD model (+46 log-loss gain, replicated). Implied team points vs actual: r = 0.40, n = 542. | **High** |
| **Player workload + goal-line role + depth chart** | Each adds a small, real improvement to TD chances, repeated on 2025 data. | **Moderate–high** (small effects) |
| **Model's top pick per team** | Hit 46.8% (125/267) in 2026 Weeks 1–9, close to what the model predicted (46%). Calibrated; at this hit rate the price has to be about +114 or longer to profit, so the pick is only as good as the price. Picks the model put at 50%+ hit 59.8% (55/92). | **Moderate** (calibration fine; profit depends on price) |
| **Rest advantage** | Correlation with covering pointed the same way in both seasons (r = +0.33 and +0.17), mostly from bye-week games; the 3+ day rule went 21-9 in 2026 but 12-13 in 2025. | **Low–moderate / preliminary**: the most promising game-level signal |
| **Fading teams on a hot cover streak** | Backing the team with the better last-3 cover record went 49-77 (38.9%, p = 0.02), i.e. fading it won 61%, but almost all of that came from 2025 (23-46); 2026 was close to even (26-31). About 20 tests were run, so one result this strong is expected by chance. | **Low**: watch it, don't bet it |
| **Ratings vs the line** (margin, EPA), travel, QB out, key injuries, division dogs | None beat the closing line in both seasons; the ratings did *worse* than a coin flip when they disagreed with the line, and the line's favorite won 69% of games vs 63–64% for either rating. The closing line already prices these. | **Low**: no evidence of an edge |
| **Prime time** | 58 prime-time games went 29-29 over/under and favorites covered 27-31; totals averaged -1.2 points vs the rest relative to the line (p = 0.52). Favorites won straight up less often in prime time (56% vs 73%). The 2026 prime-time TD jump did not repeat in 2025. | **Low / preliminary** |
| **Mid-size favorites (7–9.5)** | Covered only 16-29 (35.6%) across both seasons, while 3–6.5 favorites covered 57.8%. Not a pre-registered test; could easily be noise. | **Low / preliminary** |
| **Weather (wind, cold)** | Too few windy or cold games in Weeks 1–9 to tell, and 2026 readings are incomplete. Earlier work (`refresh/wind_study.json`) is the better reference. | **Insufficient data** |

### Data that wasn't available, and what it could change

- **Line movement / opening lines.** Only closing lines are stored. Opening-to-closing movement is a well-known signal; with it, §1 could test whether following or fading the move beats the close.
- **Player prop lines and historical anytime-TD prices** (except the family's Weeks 2–4 prices). With them, §4 could report hit rates *against the price* and actual return, which is what decides whether a pick is good.
- **Archived weather forecasts.** Game-day readings were used instead, and 2026 coverage is partial; the weather rows would firm up with forecasts.
- **2025 player picks.** The TD model needs a prior season to train on; 2024 player features weren't built, so §4 is 2026 only (n ≈ 270 team picks).
- **Routes run in 2026, offensive-line and defensive injuries.** Not in the data; they could sharpen the injury signals.
